title: Quasi-affineness reflects through a positive-degree finite locally free cover
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X,Y$ be schemes over $S$, and let $\pi:X\to Y$ be an $S$-morphism that is finite locally free of constant degree $d\geq1$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. If $X\to S$ is quasi-affine [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism], then $Y\to S$ is quasi-affine. No Noetherianity or reducedness assumption is imposed, and $d$ need not be invertible on $S$.

source.place: Tags 0BD1 (lemma-norm-quasi-affine) and 0BD2 (lemma-finite-locally-free-has-norm), applied over each affine open of S. The norm has positive degree d, including noninvertible d.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $U\subseteq S$ and write $X_U,Y_U$ for its inverse images and $f:X_U\to Y_U$ for the restriction of $\pi$. By the definition of a quasi-affine morphism, $X_U$ is quasi-affine. Restricting to an open of the target keeps the same finite, flat and locally finitely presented affine algebra charts, so $f$ is finite locally free of degree $d$; its fibres are the original fibres. It suffices to prove $Y_U$ quasi-affine for every such $U$.

source.place: Tag 0BD1 (divisors-lemma-norm-quasi-affine), applied over each affine open of S; restriction to target opens is elementary.

proof.text:
The function-norm node supplies multiplicative maps $
u$ preserving $1$ and satisfying $
u(f^\sharp a)=a^d$. The finite map $f$ has closed image. If $y
otin f(X_U)$, its open complement $V=Y_U\setminus f(X_U)$ contains $y$ but $f^{-1}V=\varnothing$. Its section ring is the zero ring, so $f^\sharp(0)=f^\sharp(1)$. Applying $
u_V$ gives $0=0^d=1$, since $d>0$, contradicting the nonzero local ring at $y$. Thus $f$ is surjective.

source.place: Section 0BCX (divisors-section-norms), observation that condition (1) forces surjectivity; Tag 0BD2.

proof.text: By the basic-open criterion, $X_U$ is quasi-compact and every point lies in an affine $(X_U)_a$ for a global function $a$. The multiplication identifications $\mathcal O_{X_U}^{\otimes n}\cong\mathcal O_{X_U}$ show, taking $n=1$, that $\mathcal O_{X_U}$ is ample in the absolute affine-section definition. The line $L=\mathcal O_{Y_U}$ is invertible (it is free of rank one). Its tensor pullback is $f^*L\cong\mathcal O_{X_U}$: locally the map is $b\otimes a\mapsto b f^\sharp(a)$, inverse $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Apply ampleness reflection to the surjective finite locally free map $f$ and this supplied line $L$. It gives $\mathcal O_{Y_U}$ ample.

source.place: Tag 0BD1 (divisors-lemma-norm-quasi-affine): O_X ample and the norm proof for O_Y; specified-line reflection follows 0BD0, 0BCY and 0BD2. Properties 01QE.

proof.text: Ampleness gives quasi-compactness of $Y_U$ and, at each $y$, an affine nonvanishing locus for a section of $\mathcal O_{Y_U}^{\otimes n}$ with $n>0$. Multiplication $a_1\otimes\cdots\otimes a_n\mapsto\prod a_i$, inverse $a\mapsto a\otimes1\otimes\cdots\otimes1$, identifies this sheaf with $\mathcal O_{Y_U}$ and preserves its nonvanishing locus. Hence the basic-open criterion makes $Y_U$ quasi-affine. As $U$ was arbitrary, $Y\to S$ is quasi-affine by definition. No division by $d$, reducedness or Noetherianity has been used.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0BD1 (divisors-lemma-norm-quasi-affine), using the existing specified-line ampleness-reflection node for the norm argument, and 0BD2. Elementary reduction over affine opens of S.
